legacy_profiles.name: DYNAMIC_EPLB
legacy_profiles.impact_detail:
DYNAMIC_EPLB enables dynamic Expert Parallel Load Balancing (EPLB) for MoE models on Ascend NPU. When set to "true" or "1", it activates a runtime load balancing mechanism that monitors expert utilization and redistributes experts across EP ranks to mitigate load imbalance. This directly improves token throughput and reduces tail latency in MoE inference by preventing individual ranks from becoming bottlenecks due to skewed expert activation patterns.
The mechanism works through several code paths: 1. In vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py:677-681, when dynamic_eplb is configured in eplb_config,
   the system asserts that DYNAMIC_EPLB (or EXPERT_MAP_RECORD) must be "true", otherwise
   it raises an assertion error. This gate ensures the environment variable is properly set
   before dynamic EPLB features activate.
2. In vllm_ascend/patch/platform/__init__.py:42-43, when DYNAMIC_EPLB is enabled, it
   conditionally imports patch_multiproc_executor, which patches the multiprocessing
   executor to support dynamic expert redistribution across worker processes.
3. In vllm_ascend/distributed/parallel_state.py:98-102, when dynamic_eplb is enabled in
   the ascend config, a dedicated _DYNAMIC_EPLB communication group is initialized using
   the same group ranks as the MC2 group. This group facilitates the all-to-all
   communication needed for expert redistribution.
4. In vllm_ascend/utils.py:1190, the dynamic_eplb communication group is assigned a
   dedicated HCCL buffer size of 100 (via _DYNAMIC_EPLB_BUFFER_SIZE), optimizing
   communication for load balancing operations.

The dynamic EPLB system collects expert heat (utilization) data at configurable intervals (expert_heat_collection_interval), runs a balancing algorithm periodically (algorithm_execution_interval), and redistributes experts with support for redundant experts (num_redundant_experts). This is particularly impactful for large MoE models like DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen3-235B where expert load imbalance can cause significant throughput degradation.

legacy_profiles.name: HCCL_INTRA_PCIE_ENABLE
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls whether HCCL (Huawei Collective Communication Library) uses PCIe for intra-node communication on Ascend NPUs. When set to "1" together with HCCL_INTRA_ROCE_ENABLE="0", it enables hierarchical communication mode for MC2 (Multi-Core Communication) operations in MoE (Mixture of Experts) models. The function `is_hierarchical_communication_enabled()` in vllm_ascend/utils.py checks this combination to determine whether to use optimized dispatch/combine operators in `TokenDispatcherWithMC2`. When enabled, the dispatcher passes `expert_scales` parameter to the MC2 dispatch/combine operators, which reduces cross-machine communication traffic and significantly improves communication performance on A2 devices. This directly affects the token dispatch path in MoE models, which is a critical performance bottleneck.

`TokenDispatcherWithMC2.__init__()` uses `is_hierarchical_communication_enabled()` to set `self.need_expert_scale`, which controls whether `expert_scales` is passed to MC2 dispatch/combine operators for optimized communication.

legacy_profiles.name: HCCL_INTRA_ROCE_ENABLE
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls whether RoCE (RDMA over Converged Ethernet) is used as the intra-server communication link between NPU groups on Ascend hardware. When set to "0" together with HCCL_INTRA_PCIE_ENABLE="1", it enables hierarchical communication mode, which triggers the MC2 (Multi-Core Communication) optimized dispatch/combine path in the MoE token dispatcher (vllm_ascend/ops/fused_moe/token_dispatcher.py:115-118). In this mode, cross-machine communication traffic is reduced and communication performance is significantly improved for MoE models on A2 series hardware. The parameter is checked in is_hierarchical_communication_enabled() (vllm_ascend/utils.py:1216-1219), which gates the MC2 hierarchy communication feature. When hierarchical communication is enabled, the token dispatcher uses expert_scales and specialized all-to-all communication patterns that bypass standard allreduce across DP groups, directly affecting token dispatch throughput and end-to-end inference latency for MoE models.

legacy_profiles.name: HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE
legacy_profiles.impact_detail:
HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE controls how HCCL (Huawei Collective Communication Library) expands collective communication operators on Ascend NPU. When set to "AIV", HCCL uses the AIVector core to directly schedule ROCE communication (FFTS+ method), which consumes fewer device streams per collective operation. This directly affects the maximum number of CUDA/ACL graph capture sizes that can be supported, because each captured graph consumes a limited pool of device resources (MAX_CAPTURE_SIZE).
In vllm_ascend/utils.py:692-705, when HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV", the code calculates a smaller parallel_factor for dense models, resulting in a higher max_num_batch_sizes. When the env var is NOT set to "AIV" (default HCCL behavior on A3 hardware uses AICPU method), the code at line 732-734 applies a more conservative formula that subtracts num_comm_groups * 40 from MAX_CAPTURE_SIZE and uses a larger parallel_factor, significantly reducing the number of supported batch sizes. Fewer capture sizes means more graph recompilations at runtime, directly hurting throughput.
Additionally, in vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_minimax_m2_config.py:118-127, for MiniMax-M2 models with ACL graph capture enabled, the code auto-sets HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE="AIV" if unset, and warns that non-AIV values "may reduce ACL graph shape coverage."
The documentation at developer_guide/performance_and_debug/optimization_and_tuning.md:182 and multiple model tutorials (Qwen3-Dense, Qwen3-Omni) explicitly recommend setting this to "AIV" for performance optimization.

legacy_profiles.name: HCCL_RDMA_RETRY_CNT
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls the number of RDMA retry attempts for HCCL communication on Ascend NPUs. It is used exclusively in the KV cache transfer timeout calculation within vllm-ascend's distributed KV transfer module. The function `get_transfer_timeout_value()` in `vllm_ascend/distributed/kv_transfer/utils/utils.py` computes the transfer timeout as: `(4.096 * (2 ** HCCL_RDMA_TIMEOUT)) * HCCL_RDMA_RETRY_CNT // 1000 + 3000` milliseconds. A higher retry count directly increases the total timeout window, which affects how long the system waits before considering a KV cache transfer as failed. During distributed inference with KV cache transfer (e.g., disaggregated prefill-decode), this timeout determines the maximum blocking time for communication operations. Setting it too low may cause premature transfer failures and request drops under network congestion, reducing throughput. Setting it too high may cause excessive blocking on slow/failed transfers, increasing tail latency. The default value of 7 combined with the default HCCL_RDMA_TIMEOUT of 20 yields a timeout of approximately 300 + 3000 = 3300 ms.

usage_locations.context: Read to compute KV transfer timeout value in get_transfer_timeout_value()

HCCL_RDMA_RETRY_CNT is ignored if ASCEND_TRANSFER_TIMEOUT environment variable is set

legacy_profiles.name: HCCL_RDMA_TIMEOUT
legacy_profiles.valid_choices: positive integer (typically 0-31, as it's used as an exponent in 2^timeout)
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: HCCL_RDMA_TIMEOUT controls the minimum retransmission timeout for RDMA communication on Ascend NPUs. In vllm-ascend, it is read in `get_transfer_timeout_value()` to compute the overall KV cache transfer timeout via the formula: `(4.096 * (2^HCCL_RDMA_TIMEOUT)) * HCCL_RDMA_RETRY_CNT // 1000 + 3000` milliseconds. This timeout governs how long the system waits for KV cache data to be transferred between NPUs during distributed inference (e.g., disaggregated prefill-decode). If the timeout is too short, transfers may fail prematurely, causing retries or connection drops that degrade throughput and increase latency. If too long, failed transfers take longer to detect, delaying recovery. The documentation also notes that HCCL_RDMA_TIMEOUT affects collective communication behavior (e.g., all-reduce, all-gather), so it has broader impact beyond just KV transfer. The parameter must satisfy: "`ASCEND_TRANSFER_TIMEOUT > RDMA_TIMEOUT * 7` where RDMA_TIMEOUT =" `4.096 * 2^HCCL_RDMA_TIMEOUT` μs.

usage_locations.context: Read in get_transfer_timeout_value() to compute KV transfer timeout; used as exponent in 2^timeout for RDMA retransmission timeout calculation.

related_parameters.name: ASCEND_TRANSFER_TIMEOUT

constraints: ASCEND_TRANSFER_TIMEOUT must be greater than (4.096 * 2^HCCL_RDMA_TIMEOUT) * HCCL_RDMA_RETRY_CNT microseconds.
HCCL_RDMA_TIMEOUT must be a valid integer; non-integer values will cause a ValueError at runtime.

tuning_advice.summary: Set HCCL_RDMA_TIMEOUT based on cluster scale and network conditions; larger clusters or slower networks need higher values to avoid premature transfer timeouts.

suggested_values.scenario: Default/small-scale deployment (few NPUs, low network latency)
suggested_values.reason: Documentation recommends 17 as a starting point; provides ~268ms RDMA timeout (4.096μs * 2^17 ≈ 537ms, times 7 retries ≈ 3.76s total).

suggested_values.scenario: Large-scale disaggregated prefill-decode with many NPUs
suggested_values.reason: Default value of 20 gives ~4.19s RDMA timeout per attempt; safer for large clusters where network congestion may cause delays.

suggested_values.scenario: High-performance RoCE network with low latency
suggested_values.reason: Lower value (~134ms per attempt) reduces detection time for genuine failures while still accommodating normal RDMA operations on fast networks.

caveats: HCCL_RDMA_TIMEOUT affects ALL collective communication (all-reduce, all-gather, etc.), not just KV transfer — changing it may impact training or other distributed operations.
The timeout grows exponentially with the value (2^timeout), so small changes have large effects: increasing from 17 to 20 multiplies the RDMA timeout by 8x.
If ASCEND_TRANSFER_TIMEOUT is set, it takes precedence over the computed value from HCCL_RDMA_TIMEOUT and HCCL_RDMA_RETRY_CNT.
Setting the timeout too low causes spurious transfer failures and retries, degrading throughput; setting it too high delays failure detection.
tuning_advice.quick_guide: Start with 17 for most deployments; increase to 20 for large clusters or if seeing RDMA timeout errors in logs.

legacy_profiles.valid_choices: comma-separated key:value pairs; supported keys: expandable_segments, max_split_size_mb, garbage_collection_threshold, page_size
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls the NPU memory allocator behavior in PyTorch Ascend. vllm-ascend automatically sets it to "expandable_segments:True" by default (platform.py:655) when sleep mode is not enabled. The expandable segments feature allows the allocator to grow memory segments dynamically, reducing memory fragmentation and OOM errors during inference. However, it is incompatible with max_split_size_mb and garbage_collection_threshold (platform.py:659-660) — if either is present, expandable_segments is not appended. The CaMemAllocator (camem.py:150) explicitly asserts that expandable_segments:True is NOT set, as it conflicts with the memory pool mechanism. The documentation also shows that max_split_size_mb can be used as an alternative strategy to reduce fragmentation by preventing large block splits (optimization_and_tuning.md:150). The choice between expandable_segments and max_split_size_mb directly impacts memory utilization efficiency and can determine whether a model fits in NPU memory at all.

usage_locations.context: Default setting: appends expandable_segments:True if not already present and no conflicting keys exist
CaMemAllocator initialization: asserts expandable_segments:True is NOT set (incompatible with memory pool)
Test fixture: explicitly sets expandable_segments:True for PD-disaggregated server tests

Test: sets expandable_segments:True for Qwen3-VL multimodal test

Test: sets expandable_segments:True for Qwen3-30B accuracy test

legacy_profiles.name: TRITON_ALL_BLOCKS_PARALLEL
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls whether Triton kernels launch all program blocks in parallel on Ascend NPU. In vllm-ascend's AscendMRotaryEmbedding.forward_triton(), when the query batch dimension (query_shape[0]) exceeds the empirical safety threshold of 65535, the code automatically sets TRITON_ALL_BLOCKS_PARALLEL=1 to prevent Triton scheduler or runtime failures on Ascend hardware. Without this flag, large Triton grids can cause kernel launch failures or severe performance degradation. The flag affects the triton_mrope kernel used for multi-dimensional rotary position embedding (MRoPE) computation, which is on the critical path for models like Qwen2-VL that use MRoPE. By enabling parallel block execution, it reduces kernel launch overhead and improves throughput for large-batch or long-sequence inference scenarios.

usage_locations.context: Checked before calling triton_mrope; if query_shape[0] > 65535 and env var is not already set to "1", the code sets it to "1" to avoid scheduler/runtime failures.

constraints: TRITON_ALL_BLOCKS_PARALLEL must be set to "1" (as a string) to take effect; any other value is treated as disabled.
This environment variable is only relevant when using the Triton-based MRoPE path on Ascend NPU (i.e., when positions.ndim == 2 and mrope_interleaved is True).

tuning_advice.summary: For large-batch or long-sequence inference with MRoPE models on Ascend NPU, set TRITON_ALL_BLOCKS_PARALLEL=1 to prevent Triton kernel launch failures and improve throughput. The vllm-ascend code auto-enables it when the batch dimension exceeds 65535, but manually setting it can provide stability for borderline cases.

suggested_values.scenario: High-throughput serving with large batch sizes or long sequences using MRoPE models (e.g., Qwen2-VL) on Ascend NPU
suggested_values.reason: Prevents Triton scheduler/runtime failures when the query batch dimension is large. Even when below the 65535 threshold, enabling this flag can reduce kernel launch overhead and improve throughput stability.

suggested_values.scenario: Low-latency serving with small batch sizes and short sequences
suggested_values.reason: For small grids, parallel block execution may introduce unnecessary overhead. The default behavior (disabled) is sufficient and avoids potential resource contention.

caveats: The vllm-ascend code automatically sets this flag when query_shape[0] > 65535, so manual setting is primarily useful for borderline cases or to ensure consistent behavior across deployments.
This flag only affects the Triton-based MRoPE path; it has no effect on the npu_mrope (torch_npu) fallback path used when mrope_section is not [16, 24, 24] or when Triton is unavailable.
Setting this flag may increase memory usage slightly due to parallel block execution, though the impact is typically negligible compared to model weights and KV cache.
tuning_advice.quick_guide: Set TRITON_ALL_BLOCKS_PARALLEL=1 for MRoPE models with large batches on Ascend NPU; leave unset for small-scale inference.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_ALLOW_CHUNKED_LOCAL_ATTN_WITH_HYBRID_KV_CACHE
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls whether the Hybrid KV cache manager is allowed to be used together with chunked local attention (attention_chunk_size is set). When set to 0 (false), the hybrid KV cache manager is forcibly disabled for models using chunked local attention, falling back to the standard KV cache manager. The standard KV cache manager uses more memory because it cannot share KV cache blocks between full-attention and local-attention layers in hybrid models (e.g., Llama4). Enabling this flag (default true) allows the hybrid KV cache manager to operate, which saves KV cache memory and enables longer context lengths, but the upstream code explicitly warns of a known latency regression when combining chunked local attention with the hybrid KV cache manager. On Ascend NPU, this tradeoff is equally relevant: "the hybrid KV cache manager reduces memory pressure (critical for" NPU HBM), but the latency regression may be more or less pronounced depending on CANN's attention kernel efficiency. The parameter is checked in vllm/config/vllm.py:1329 during scheduler configuration initialization.

usage_locations.context: During scheduler config initialization, checks if chunked local attention is enabled (attention_chunk_size is not None) and if speculative decoding with Eagle is not active. If VLLM_ALLOW_CHUNKED_LOCAL_ATTN_WITH_HYBRID_KV_CACHE is false, the hybrid KV cache manager is disabled with a warning log.

related_parameters.name: attention_chunk_size
related_parameters.relation: This parameter only takes effect when attention_chunk_size is set (chunked local attention is enabled). Without chunked local attention, the hybrid KV cache manager operates normally regardless of this env var.

related_parameters.relation: If the user explicitly disables the hybrid KV cache manager via --disable-kv-cache-manager, this env var has no effect — the hybrid manager is already off.

related_parameters.name: speculative_config (Eagle)
related_parameters.relation: When speculative decoding with Eagle is active and chunked local attention is enabled, the hybrid KV cache manager is unconditionally disabled, overriding this env var.

constraints: This env var has no effect if attention_chunk_size is not set (chunked local attention is not enabled).
This env var has no effect if speculative decoding with Eagle is active and chunked local attention is enabled — hybrid KV cache manager is unconditionally disabled in that case.
This env var has no effect if the user explicitly disables the hybrid KV cache manager via --disable-kv-cache-manager.

tuning_advice.summary: Enable (default) to save KV cache memory on hybrid models like Llama4 at the cost of a known latency regression; disable if latency is more critical than memory savings.

suggested_values.scenario: Running hybrid models (e.g., Llama4) with chunked local attention on Ascend NPU where memory is constrained and longer context is needed.
suggested_values.reason: The hybrid KV cache manager shares KV cache blocks between full-attention and local-attention layers, significantly reducing KV cache memory usage and enabling longer context lengths. The default value (true) is appropriate for memory-constrained NPU scenarios.

suggested_values.scenario: Running hybrid models with chunked local attention where latency is the primary concern and memory is sufficient.
suggested_values.reason: Upstream code explicitly documents a latency regression when combining chunked local attention with the hybrid KV cache manager. Disabling it falls back to the standard KV cache manager, which avoids this regression at the cost of higher memory usage.

caveats:
The latency regression mentioned in the upstream code is GPU-observed; on Ascend NPU the magnitude may differ due to CANN's attention kernel implementation. Benchmark both settings on your specific NPU hardware.
This flag only affects hybrid models (models with both full-attention and local-attention layers, such as Llama4). For non-hybrid models, the hybrid KV cache manager behavior is unaffected by this flag.
The upstream TODO comment indicates this flag is temporary and will be removed once the latency regression is resolved — expect behavior changes in future vLLM versions.
tuning_advice.quick_guide: Keep the default (true) for memory savings on Ascend NPU; set to 0 only if latency regression is confirmed and unacceptable for your workload.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls whether vLLM allows the user to set --max-model-len to a value exceeding the maximum sequence length derived from the model's config.json (e.g., max_position_embeddings). When set to true, the ValueError that normally blocks such overrides is downgraded to a warning, and the user-specified max_model_len is accepted. On Ascend NPU, this directly affects KV cache allocation size (larger max_model_len consumes more HBM), the number of tokens that can be batched, and whether long-context inference scenarios (e.g., 128K+ tokens) are even possible. The vllm-ascend test suite (conftest.py, long_sequence tests) explicitly sets VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 to enable max_model_len values far beyond the model's default, which is essential for testing chunked prefill with context parallelism on Ascend hardware. Without this flag, attempting to serve long sequences on Ascend would fail at startup with a ValueError.

usage_locations.context: During model config initialization, checks if user-specified max_model_len exceeds derived_max_model_len. If VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN is true, logs a warning instead of raising ValueError, allowing the override.

The env var only bypasses the startup check; it does not guarantee the model can actually handle the extended sequence length correctly.

suggested_values.reason: No need to bypass the safety check; the default behavior prevents accidental misconfiguration that could produce NaN outputs or crashes.

suggested_values.scenario: Long-context inference on Ascend NPU with RoPE-scaled models (e.g., Qwen3 with YaRN, models with extended context via rope_theta/factor)
suggested_values.reason: Required to set --max-model-len beyond the config.json limit. The vllm-ascend test suite uses this for all long-sequence tests (128K+ tokens) with chunked prefill and context parallelism on Ascend.

suggested_values.scenario: Testing or benchmarking long sequences on Ascend NPU
suggested_values.reason: The vllm-ascend E2E test infrastructure unconditionally sets this to enable flexible max_model_len configuration during testing.

caveats:
On Ascend NPU, setting an excessively large max_model_len without corresponding RoPE scaling parameters (rope_theta, rope_type, factor) will produce NaN outputs for positions beyond the original training length.
Increasing max_model_len significantly increases KV cache memory consumption. On Ascend NPU with limited HBM, you may need to reduce --gpu-memory-utilization or increase --tensor-parallel-size to distribute the KV cache across multiple NPUs.
The vllm-ascend plugin does not override or modify this env var's behavior; it inherits the upstream vLLM logic directly. The flag is used extensively in vllm-ascend tests but has no Ascend-specific code path.
tuning_advice.quick_guide: Set VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 only for long-context models with proper RoPE scaling; otherwise leave it disabled (default) to catch misconfiguration early.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_ALLOW_RUNTIME_LORA_UPDATING
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable enables dynamic loading and unloading of LoRA adapters at runtime via the API server (POST /v1/load_lora_adapter, POST /v1/unload_lora_adapter). When enabled, the server can resolve unrecognized model names by attempting to load them as LoRA adapters from local cache (VLLM_LORA_RESOLVER_CACHE_DIR) or remote HF repos (VLLM_LORA_RESOLVER_HF_REPO_LIST). The primary performance impact is on memory: enabling runtime LoRA updating requires reserving additional GPU/NPU memory headroom for potential new adapter weights, and each loaded adapter consumes memory proportional to its rank and the base model's layer sizes. There is also a minor latency impact on first-use of an unrecognized model name, as the adapter must be downloaded and loaded synchronously. On Ascend NPU, the memory overhead of LoRA adapters follows the same pattern as GPU, but the available device memory may be more constrained, making the memory reservation more impactful. This parameter does not directly affect compute throughput for requests that use already-loaded adapters.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls whether vLLM uses PyTorch symmetric memory (torch.distributed._symm_mem) for tensor-parallel allreduce operations on CUDA GPUs. When enabled (default), the SymmMemCommunicator is used for TP allreduce, which can reduce latency by leveraging hardware multicast capabilities on supported NVIDIA GPUs (SM90+). On Ascend NPU, this mechanism is NOT applicable — Ascend uses HCCL for collective communication, and the SymmMemCommunicator path is CUDA-specific. The parameter is read in cuda_communicator.py:53 and only affects the CUDA communicator path. On Ascend, the communication backend is handled by HCCL via the vllm-ascend plugin, which does not reference this environment variable. Therefore, this parameter has no direct effect on Ascend NPU performance. However, leaving it at the default value (1) may cause harmless warning messages during initialization if symmetric memory is unavailable, which is always the case on Ascend.

usage_locations.context: Reads VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM to decide whether to use SymmMemCommunicator for TP allreduce. Only applies when unique_name contains "tp".
Logs a warning suggesting users set VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0 if symmetric memory initialization fails.
Overrides VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM to "0" when batch invariance mode is enabled, to ensure deterministic allreduce behavior.

related_parameters.name: VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_FLASHINFER
related_parameters.relation: Alternative allreduce backend for CUDA; mutually exclusive in practice with symmetric memory allreduce. Both are CUDA-specific and irrelevant on Ascend.

related_parameters.relation: When enabled, VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM is forcibly set to 0 to ensure deterministic communication.

constraints: Symmetric memory allreduce is only available for tensor-parallel (TP) groups, not for other process groups.
Symmetric memory requires NVIDIA GPU hardware support (SM90+ with multicast capability); it is not available on Ascend NPU.

tuning_advice.summary: On Ascend NPU, this parameter has no effect on communication performance. Set to 0 to suppress harmless initialization warnings.

suggested_values.scenario: All Ascend NPU deployments
suggested_values.reason: Symmetric memory allreduce is a CUDA-specific feature and is not supported on Ascend NPU. Setting to 0 avoids unnecessary warning messages during SymmMemCommunicator initialization.

caveats:
On Ascend NPU, tensor-parallel allreduce is handled by HCCL via the vllm-ascend plugin. This environment variable does not affect HCCL communication in any way.
Leaving this at the default value (1) on Ascend will cause a one-time warning log about symmetric memory initialization failure, but does not affect functionality or performance.
tuning_advice.quick_guide: Set VLLM_ALLREDUCE_USE_SYMM_MEM=0 on Ascend NPU to suppress irrelevant CUDA-specific warnings.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_ASCEND_APPLY_DSV4_PATCH
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: When enabled (set to "1"), this environment variable activates a collection of DeepSeek V4-specific patches in vllm-ascend. The most performance-critical change is in KV cache management: "it forces the use of" AscendHybridKVCacheCoordinator (patch_kv_cache_coordinator.py:290-303), which implements a MultiBlockPool strategy for KV cache allocation. This hybrid coordinator is specifically designed for DeepSeek V4's DSA (Dual-Stream Attention) architecture with context parallelism (CP), enabling efficient KV cache interleaving across CP ranks. Additionally, it imports speculative decoding patches (patch_speculative_config) that are tailored for DeepSeek V4's MTP (Multi-Token Prediction) layers. The patch is always used together with VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASHCOMM1 in test configurations, suggesting these two optimizations are complementary for DeepSeek V4 inference. Without this patch, DeepSeek V4 models fall back to standard KV cache coordinators that may not handle DSA CP interleaving correctly, potentially causing memory fragmentation, reduced throughput, or incorrect results under context parallelism.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_ASCEND_BALANCE_SCHEDULING
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: When enabled, balance scheduling modifies the vLLM v1 scheduler behavior to separate prefill and decode requests into distinct scheduling sessions, rather than processing them simultaneously in a single session (the default chunked-prefill behavior). This is implemented via a monkey-patch in vllm_ascend/patch/platform/patch_balance_schedule.py that patches EngineCoreProc.run_engine_core and the Scheduler class. The separation can improve output throughput and reduce TPOT (Time Per Output Token) in some scenarios, but may degrade TTFT (Time To First Token). The feature is specifically noted as not recommended for PD-disaggregated (prefill-decode separated) deployments.

usage_locations.context: Reads the env var via _get_config_value and stores it as self.enable_balance_scheduling. Also checks for incompatibility with profiling_chunk_config — raises ValueError if both are enabled simultaneously.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_BATCH_MEMCPY
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls whether the vllm-ascend C++ extension is compiled with support for `aclrtMemcpyBatchAsync`, a CANN API that performs batched memory copies between host and device. The primary use case is KV cache offloading — when the KV cache is swapped between NPU HBM and CPU RAM (e.g., under memory pressure or for prefix caching), batched memcpy can significantly reduce the overhead of many small transfers by issuing them as a single batch operation. Enabling this feature (value "1") forces the compile-time inclusion of the batched memcpy code path. Disabling it (value "0") forces exclusion. When unset (null), the CMake build system auto-detects whether the installed CANN headers support the API. The performance impact is medium because it only affects offloading scenarios — if KV cache offloading is not active, this parameter has no runtime effect. However, when offloading IS active, the difference between batched and individual memcpy calls can be substantial for latency-sensitive workloads.

usage_locations.context: During vllm-ascend C++ extension build, the env var value is passed to CMake as -DVLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_BATCH_MEMCPY. When None, the flag is omitted and CMake auto-detects from CANN headers.
Defined in the env_variables dict with lazy evaluation. Returns the raw string value or None if unset.

related_parameters.name: VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_MLAPO
related_parameters.relation: Both are vllm-ascend env vars that control Ascend-specific optimizations at different levels — MLAPO affects DeepSeek W8A8 model execution, while BATCH_MEMCPY affects KV cache offloading infrastructure.

related_parameters.name: --swap-space
related_parameters.relation: The vLLM CLI parameter that controls CPU swap space size for KV cache offloading. VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_BATCH_MEMCPY optimizes the transfer mechanism when swap-space is actually used.

constraints: This is a compile-time flag — changing its value requires rebuilding the vllm-ascend C++ extension (pip install -e . or similar).
The auto-detection path (None) depends on the installed CANN version; if CANN headers do not expose aclrtMemcpyBatchAsync, the feature is silently disabled.

tuning_advice.summary: Enable batched memcpy if your deployment uses KV cache offloading (swap-space > 0) and your CANN version supports it; otherwise leave unset for auto-detection.

suggested_values.scenario: KV cache offloading is active (--swap-space > 0) and CANN version supports aclrtMemcpyBatchAsync
suggested_values.reason: Forces the batched memcpy code path, reducing per-transfer overhead when KV cache blocks are swapped between NPU HBM and CPU RAM. This directly improves latency during prefill-decode transitions that trigger offloading.

suggested_values.scenario: KV cache offloading is not used (--swap-space 0 or default)
suggested_values.reason: The batched memcpy code path has no effect when offloading is inactive. Leaving it unset allows auto-detection and avoids unnecessary compile-time dependencies.

suggested_values.scenario: CANN version is known to have buggy or missing aclrtMemcpyBatchAsync support
suggested_values.reason: Explicitly disables the feature to prevent compilation errors or runtime crashes from a broken/missing CANN API.

caveats: This is a compile-time flag, not a runtime toggle. After changing the value, you must rebuild the vllm-ascend extension.
When set to '1' but the CANN headers lack aclrtMemcpyBatchAsync, the CMake build will fail — check CANN compatibility first.
The performance benefit only materializes when KV cache offloading actually occurs; for pure HBM-resident workloads, this flag has zero impact.
tuning_advice.quick_guide: Set to "1" if you use --swap-space and your CANN supports aclrtMemcpyBatchAsync; otherwise leave unset.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASHCOMM1
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls whether FlashComm1 optimization is enabled during tensor-parallel execution on Ascend NPUs. When enabled (set to "1"), it activates the Sequence Parallelism (SP) code path in vllm-ascend, which fuses communication and computation to reduce all-reduce overhead in tensor-parallel layers. The `enable_sp()` function in vllm_ascend/utils.py reads this variable (or its `additional_config` equivalent) and returns a boolean that gates SP behavior throughout the model execution. FlashComm1 is particularly effective under high concurrency, where communication latency becomes a bottleneck. It is also a prerequisite for DSA CP (DeepSeek Attention Context Parallelism), which requires SP to be enabled and will raise a ValueError if DSA CP is requested without FlashComm1. The parameter is deprecated in favor of `additional_config.enable_flashcomm1`, but the env var still takes effect through the `_get_config_value` fallback chain in `ascend_config.py`.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FUSED_MC2
legacy_profiles.impact_detail:
Controls whether fused MC2 (Model Communication Combine) operators replace standard ALLTOALL + MC2 communication in MoE layers on Ascend NPU. Three modes: - "0 (default): standard ALLTOALL + MC2 path, no fusion." - 1: "enables `dispatch_ffn_combine` operator, which fuses ALLTOALL and MC2"
  for MoE layers with W8A8 quantization, EP<=32, non-MTP, non-dynamic-EPLB.
- 2: "enables `dispatch_gmm_combine_decode` operator, which fuses MC2 for"
  decode-phase MoE layers with W8A8 (MTP layers must also be W8A8).

The fusion eliminates separate communication and computation kernels, reducing kernel launch overhead and improving data locality on the NPU. This directly reduces per-token latency and increases throughput for MoE models (e.g., DeepSeek, GLM-5) by overlapping or combining communication with computation. The effect is most pronounced at high concurrency where communication overhead dominates.
The parameter is read in `vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py:146-151` via `_get_config_value`, which checks both the `additional_config` dict key `enable_fused_mc2` and the env var `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FUSED_MC2`, with `additional_config` taking precedence. It is validated in `vllm_ascend/platform.py:670-674`: if both `enable_mc2_hierarchy_comm` and `enable_fused_mc2` are enabled, a ValueError is raised because fused MC2 operators are incompatible with hierarchy communication (ROCE-based inter-node dispatch/combine).

usage_locations.context: Environment variable definition with docstring describing three modes and their constraints.
Config loading: reads from additional_config dict or env var, stores as AscendConfig.enable_fused_mc2.
Runtime validation: raises ValueError if fused MC2 is enabled together with hierarchy communication.

suggested_values.reason: Mode 2 uses `dispatch_gmm_combine_decode` specifically optimized for decode nodes, providing additional fusion benefits for decode-dominated serving scenarios.

suggested_values.reason: Fused MC2 operators have strict W8A8 and architecture requirements. Disabling avoids startup errors and falls back to the standard ALLTOALL+MC2 path.

Mode 2 only accelerates decode nodes; prefill nodes still use the standard path. For mixed prefill/decode workloads, mode 1 may provide more balanced benefits.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_MATMUL_ALLREDUCE
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: When enabled, this parameter activates a MatmulAllReduce fusion kernel that fuses the matrix multiplication and all-reduce communication operations during the prefill phase when tensor parallelism (TP) is enabled. On Ascend NPUs, all-reduce communication between TP ranks can be a significant bottleneck. By fusing the matmul computation with the all-reduce communication, the kernel overlaps computation and communication, reducing the overall latency of the prefill phase and improving throughput. The feature is specifically supported on Ascend A2 hardware (Ascend910B) and is noted to achieve better performance in eager mode rather than graph mode. The parameter is read in vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py:143 via the _get_config_value method, which checks both the additional_config dict (key: enable_matmul_allreduce) and the environment variable, with additional_config taking precedence. The env var is deprecated in favor of the additional_config key.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_NZ
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: Controls whether model weights are cast to FRACTAL_NZ format on Ascend NPU. FRACTAL_NZ is a Da Vinci architecture-specific memory layout that can improve compute efficiency for matrix operations but may increase memory usage. The parameter has three modes: - "0: Disabled — weights remain in their original format." - "1: Only quantized weights (e.g., W8A8) are converted to NZ (default)." - "2: BF16/FP16 weights are also converted to NZ whenever possible." On 310P devices, NZ conversion is always applied regardless of this setting. On non-310P devices, the mode is respected. FP32 weights are never converted. The conversion happens in `maybe_trans_nz()` via `torch_npu.npu_format_cast()`. According to release notes, mode 2 was disabled by default for float weights due to performance regressions in some cases, but users can still enable it if it benefits their specific workload.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_ASCEND_FUSION_OP_TRANSPOSE_KV_CACHE_BY_BLOCK
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls whether a fused custom operator is used during KV cache reformatting in PD (prefill-decode) disaggregation scenarios on Ascend NPUs. When enabled (default), the Mooncake KV transfer connectors (both standard and hybrid) call `reformat_kv_cache_with_fused_op` instead of the generic `reformat_kv_cache` path. The fused operator performs transpose-by-block operations on KV cache tensors in a single optimized kernel, reducing the number of kernel launches and device-host synchronization points. This directly reduces the latency of KV cache transfer between prefill and decode nodes, which is on the critical path for time-to-first-token in disaggregated serving. Disabling it falls back to a non-fused implementation that may use multiple smaller operations, increasing overhead. The parameter has no effect outside PD disaggregation scenarios (i.e., when KV transfer is not active or when neither `need_cat_cache` nor `need_nz_cache` is true).

usage_locations.context: Standard Mooncake connector reads this env var to decide whether to use the fused `reformat_kv_cache_with_fused_op` or the generic `reformat_kv_cache` when reformatting KV cache blocks after transfer.
Hybrid Mooncake connector reads this env var to decide whether to use the fused `reformat_kv_cache_with_fused_op` or the generic `reformat_kv_cache` when reformatting KV cache blocks after transfer.
AscendConfig reads this env var and stores it as `enable_transpose_kv_cache_by_block`, which can also be set via `additional_config` dict.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
legacy_profiles.impact_detail:
When VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1, vLLM and vllm-ascend enforce deterministic computation regardless of batch composition. This triggers a cascade of changes across multiple subsystems that collectively reduce performance but guarantee bitwise reproducibility:
1. **Custom all-reduce disabled** (vllm/config/parallel.py:919): `disable_custom_all_reduce` is forced to True, falling back to standard NCCL/HCCL all-reduce which is slower than custom all-reduce kernels.
2. **Cascade attention disabled** (vllm/config/vllm.py:1269-1272): `disable_cascade_attn` is forced to True, preventing the use of cascade attention optimizations that improve throughput for mixed-length batches.
3. **FlashAttention version downgrade** (vllm/v1/attention/backends/fa_utils.py:144): FA4 is downgraded to FA2 because FA4 uses batch-shape-dependent scheduling heuristics that break batch invariance.
4. **AOT scheduling disabled** (vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py:414): Ahead-of-time scheduling is disabled because the schedule varies with max_seqlen_q/k, forcing runtime scheduling which adds overhead.
5. **FlashAttention max_num_splits forced to 1** (vllm/v1/attention/backends/flash_attn.py:445, vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/flashattn_mla.py:157): Prevents split-kernel execution that improves throughput for long sequences.
6. **FlashInfer fixed split sizes** (vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py:560-567): Decode split size fixed to 2048, prefill split size fixed to 4096, and split-kv disabled. Larger workspace buffer allocated (vllm/v1/attention/backends/flashinfer.py:751-752).
7. **FlexAttention kernel options** (vllm/v1/attention/backends/flex_attention.py:1173-1177): BLOCK_M and BLOCK_N forced to 16 with IS_DIVISIBLE=False, reducing kernel efficiency.
8. **Ascend-specific: custom ops disabled** (vllm_ascend/utils.py:374): All custom Ascend operators are disabled, falling back to generic implementations.
9. **Ascend-specific: async exponential disabled** (vllm_ascend/ascend_config.py:225): The async exponential sampling optimization is disabled because it makes batch_invariant mode non-functional.
10. **Ascend-specific: sampler fallback** (vllm_ascend/sample/sampler.py:135, vllm_ascend/_310p/sample/sampler.py:63): Ascend-optimized sampling kernels are bypassed in favor of vLLM's upstream implementation.
The net effect is significantly reduced throughput and increased latency, with potentially higher memory usage due to larger workspace buffers. This mode should only be used for debugging or when deterministic results are strictly required.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_CACHE_ROOT
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: VLLM_CACHE_ROOT controls the root directory for all vLLM cache files, including torch.compile cache artifacts, GPU P2P access caches, model info caches, XLA caches, and asset caches. On Ascend NPU, the most performance-critical subdirectory is `torch_compile_cache`, which stores compiled graph artifacts generated by the inductor backend. When torch.compile is enabled (via compilation_config), vLLM computes a hash based on environment, config, source code, and compiler version, then stores compiled graphs under `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT/torch_compile_cache/<hash>/`. On cache hit, the compilation step is skipped entirely, significantly reducing cold-start latency. On cache miss, the full compilation pipeline runs, which can take minutes for large models. The cache also affects AOT compilation artifacts stored under `torch_aot_compile/`. Additionally, GPU P2P access check results are cached under this root, avoiding repeated peer-to-peer capability probing on subsequent launches. While vllm-ascend does not override this parameter, the compilation cache behavior is equally relevant on Ascend NPU because CANN graph compilation is expensive and caching avoids redundant recompilation across restarts.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_COMPILE_CACHE_SAVE_FORMAT
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls the on-disk format of the torch.compile cache artifacts. When set to "binary" (default), compiled graphs are saved as a single binary file, which is multiprocess-safe — critical when multiple vllm serve processes share the same cache directory. When set to "unpacked", the cache is saved as a directory structure, enabling inspection and debugging of Inductor's generated code but introducing race conditions under concurrent access. The parameter does not affect the compilation process itself or the runtime execution of compiled graphs; it only changes how cache artifacts are serialized to disk. On Ascend NPU, torch.compile is used via the vLLM Inductor backend (compilation mode 3), and cache reuse accelerates cold-start latency. The save format has no direct impact on steady-state throughput or memory usage, but "unpacked" mode can cause cache corruption in multi-process deployments, leading to cache misses and recompilation overhead that degrades cold-start performance.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: When VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=0 (default), vLLM caches torch.compile artifacts (Inductor compiled graphs and AOT compiled functions) to disk under VLLM_CACHE_ROOT/torch_compile_cache/. On subsequent warm starts, these cached artifacts are loaded from disk instead of being recompiled, dramatically reducing startup latency. When set to 1, all compilation caching is disabled — every warm start must recompile all torch.compile graphs from scratch. The code at vllm/compilation/compiler_interface.py:409 explicitly warns that disabling the cache "will greatly increase vLLM server warm start times." This affects both the Inductor backend path (vllm/compilation/backends.py:1076) and the AOT compile path (vllm/compilation/decorators.py:564,689). On Ascend NPU, where CANN graph compilation is already expensive, forcing torch.compile recompilation on every restart compounds startup overhead significantly. The parameter does not affect steady-state inference throughput or latency — only startup/warm-up time. No vllm-ascend override was found; the upstream behavior applies directly on Ascend.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_DISABLE_PYNCCL
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: When VLLM_DISABLE_PYNCCL is set to true, the PyNcclCommunicator is disabled and vLLM falls back to using torch.distributed for all-reduce operations (see vllm/distributed/device_communicators/pynccl.py:91). On Ascend NPU, torch.distributed uses HCCL as the communication backend. PyNCCL is a lightweight NCCL wrapper that avoids Python GIL overhead and torch.distributed initialization costs. Disabling it forces all collective communication through the heavier torch.distributed path, which can increase per-step communication latency and reduce throughput, especially in tensor-parallel configurations where frequent all-reduce operations occur. The impact is most pronounced during decode phases with small message sizes, where PyNCCL's lower overhead provides a measurable advantage.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM
legacy_profiles.impact_detail:
This environment variable controls whether MoE (Mixture of Experts) shared experts are executed in a separate CUDA/HCCL stream to overlap with other operations. When set to 1 (disabled), shared experts run sequentially in the default stream, eliminating stream synchronization overhead but also removing any potential overlap benefit. When set to 0 (enabled), shared experts are dispatched to an auxiliary stream via aux_stream(), allowing concurrent execution with other kernels.
On Ascend NPU, vllm-ascend unconditionally sets this to "1" in platform.py:32, meaning the separate stream path is ALWAYS disabled regardless of user configuration. This is a hard override — any user attempt to set VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM=0 is silently ignored because the platform module executes before user env vars are fully processed. The comment in platform.py:31 indicates this is a temporary workaround ("todo: please remove it when solve cuda hard code in vllm"), suggesting that the upstream CUDA stream mechanism is not yet compatible with Ascend's HCCL stream model.
The performance impact is classified as "low" because on Ascend this parameter is effectively non-functional — it is always forced to 1. The theoretical performance difference (overlap vs sequential execution) cannot be realized on Ascend until the platform override is removed and HCCL stream support is validated.

CPU platform also forces VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM=1 since CPU has no CUDA stream concept. This is the same pattern vllm-ascend follows for Ascend.

However, it does not directly affect steady-state inference throughput or per-request latency. The parameter only has an effect when elastic EP scaling is triggered via the `scale_elastic_ep()` API. legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_ELASTIC_EP_SCALE_UP_LAUNCH
legacy_profiles.impact_detail:
This environment variable is an internal flag used by vLLM's elastic expert parallelism (EP) scale-up mechanism. When set to 1, it signals that the current engine instance is being launched as part of a scale-up operation (adding more data-parallel ranks to a running deployment).    uniproc_executor.py:62), it calls elastic_ep_execute("load_model") instead of
   the standard load_model(), which handles the distributed synchronization needed

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_ENABLE_FLA_PACKED_RECURRENT_DECODE
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls whether the Gated DeltaNet (GDN) linear attention layer uses a "packed recurrent decode" optimization during the decode phase. When enabled (default), the `GatedDeltaNetLinearAttention` layer sets `self.enable_packed_recurrent_decode = True`, which activates a specialized code path in `ChunkGatedDeltaRule` that processes multiple sequences in a packed/batched manner during recurrent decoding. This optimization is specific to models using GDN linear attention (e.g., Qwen3-Next architecture). The performance impact is limited to the decode phase of GDN-based models and does not affect prefill or other attention mechanisms. On Ascend NPU, the effect depends on whether the packed recurrent decode kernel is well-optimized for the Da Vinci architecture — if the kernel relies on operations that are not efficiently mapped to Ascend, disabling this flag may actually improve performance by falling back to a more generic but better-optimized code path. No vllm-ascend override or Ascend-specific handling was found for this parameter.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_ENABLE_PREGRAD_PASSES
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls whether PyTorch Inductor's pre-grad passes are executed during torch.compile. When enabled (default), pre-grad passes run even on cache hits, adding approximately O(1s) to cold compile times. When disabled, the `_recursive_pre_grad_passes` function is patched to a no-op (identity function), skipping these passes entirely. The code comments explicitly state that "Inductor's pre-grad passes don't do anything for vLLM," so disabling them reduces compilation overhead without affecting model correctness. This affects startup/warmup latency (cold compile time) but has no impact on steady-state inference throughput or memory usage. On Ascend NPU, the effect is identical to upstream since this is a PyTorch-level compilation optimization that applies regardless of backend hardware. The parameter is automatically bypassed (pre-grad passes enabled) when PyTorch >= 2.12.0.dev because the upstream fix (pytorch#174502) resolves the cache-hit overhead issue.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls whether the V1 LLMEngine uses multiprocessing mode (spawning a separate process for the engine core) or runs the engine core in the same process as the caller. When enabled (default), the engine core runs in a child process via multiprocessing.Process, which provides process isolation and avoids GIL contention between the engine core and the Python caller. When disabled, the engine core runs in-process, which can affect the random state of the launching Python process and reduces process isolation. On Ascend NPU, the impact is indirect but meaningful: multiprocessing mode affects how the executor and workers are initialized, which in turn influences NPU memory allocation patterns and inter-process communication overhead. The parameter is read in vllm/v1/engine/llm_engine.py:148 and :165 to set the multiprocess_mode flag passed to the LLMEngine constructor. It is also checked in vllm/config/parallel.py:828 where it is forcibly set to "0" when using the "external_launcher" distributed executor backend, and in vllm/v1/executor/uniproc_executor.py:168 where it is asserted to be False for deterministic execution with ExecutorWithExternalLauncher.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls the precision mode used by PyTorch for float32 matrix multiplications via torch.set_float32_matmul_precision(). On Ascend NPU, this setting is applied in the v1 worker initialization path (vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py:124-125) and affects all subsequent matmul operations in the model forward pass. The three modes map to: 'highest' (full IEEE FP32, no precision loss), 'high' (TF32 tensor cores on CUDA, but on Ascend NPU this may fall back to FP32 or use a CANN-specific fast path depending on the operator), and 'medium' (bfloat16-like precision for matmul accumulation). On Ascend NPU, the actual behavior depends on the CANN operator implementation and the specific Da Vinci architecture support for mixed-precision matmul. Lower precision modes can significantly accelerate matrix multiplications at the cost of numerical accuracy, directly affecting both token generation latency and overall throughput. No vllm-ascend override was found for this parameter, so the upstream vLLM behavior applies as-is on Ascend hardware.

On Ascend NPU, the AOT compilation path (torch.compile with Inductor backend) is the same as upstream — vllm-ascend does not override or modify this parameter's behavior. The performance impact is low because this parameter only changes error handling behavior during model loading; it does not affect the actual compilation process, runtime execution, or memory usage. It is also excluded from the torch.compile cache key (listed in ignored_factors at vllm/envs.py:1891), confirming it has no effect on compilation output.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: Controls the memory layout of the KV cache tensor, which directly affects attention kernel performance and memory access patterns. An incompatible layout can cause the backend to fall back to a slower kernel path or fail entirely. On Ascend, the vllm-ascend plugin's attention backend will similarly have a preferred layout; forcing an unsupported layout may degrade performance or cause errors.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_MEDIA_CACHE
legacy_profiles.valid_choices: any valid filesystem path string, or empty string to disable
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: VLLM_MEDIA_CACHE controls the directory path for caching media files (images, video, audio) fetched from URLs during multimodal inference. When set to a non-empty writable directory path, vLLM enables a disk-based LRU cache for downloaded media, avoiding repeated network fetches for the same URLs across requests. This can reduce end-to-end request latency for multimodal workloads where the same media URLs are referenced repeatedly (e.g., benchmark suites, repeated queries against a fixed image set). The cache is managed with size and TTL limits controlled by sibling env vars VLLM_MEDIA_CACHE_MAX_SIZE_MB and VLLM_MEDIA_CACHE_TTL_HOURS. When empty (default), caching is completely disabled and every request triggers a fresh network fetch. This parameter is upstream vLLM functionality with no vllm-ascend override — it behaves identically on Ascend NPU as on GPU. It is explicitly excluded from torch.compile cache key computation (vllm/envs.py:1913), confirming it has no impact on model compilation or execution graph. Performance impact is limited to I/O-bound multimodal request preprocessing, not the NPU compute path.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_MEMORY_PROFILER_ESTIMATE_CUDAGRAPHS
legacy_profiles.impact_detail:
This environment variable controls whether CUDA graph memory estimation is applied during the memory profiling phase of vLLM initialization. When enabled (default), the profiler measures the additional GPU memory consumed by CUDA graphs and subtracts this from the available KV cache budget. This results in more accurate KV cache allocation, preventing OOM errors at the cost of slightly reduced KV cache capacity. When disabled, CUDA graph memory is not accounted for, which may lead to a larger KV cache allocation but risks OOM when CUDA graphs are actually instantiated.
On Ascend NPU, the behavior depends on whether the vllm-ascend plugin uses CUDA graph equivalents (NPU graphs via CANN). The code path in vllm/v1/worker/gpu_worker.py shows that cudagraph_memory_estimate is only computed when the platform is CUDA (line 403: `current_platform.is_cuda()`). On Ascend NPU, this condition is false, so `cudagraph_memory_estimate` remains 0 regardless of this env var setting. However, the env var still affects the logging logic at line 471, which may print misleading suggestions about adjusting --gpu-memory-utilization.
The vllm-ascend plugin does not override or redefine this env var. Its effect on Ascend is therefore limited to the logging path, but the memory estimation itself is a no-op because the CUDA graph profiling code is guarded by `is_cuda()`.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_MOONCAKE_ABORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT
legacy_profiles.impact_detail:
This environment variable controls the timeout (in seconds) for the MooncakeConnector in a disaggregated prefill-decode (PD) setup. It is used in two distinct code paths:
1. **vllm-ascend (Ascend NPU)**: In `mooncake_connector.py` and `mooncake_hybrid_connector.py`, the timeout governs how long a "delayed free request" is held before its resources (KV cache blocks) are forcibly released. When a request's delay exceeds this timeout, the request is removed from the processing queue and its blocks are freed, preventing memory leaks on the producer side. This directly affects memory pressure: a shorter timeout frees memory faster but risks prematurely aborting requests that are still being processed; a longer timeout preserves requests longer but may cause memory exhaustion under high load.
2. **vllm upstream (GPU)**: In `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py`, the timeout is used in `asyncio.wait()` calls when waiting for the producer side to signal readiness for KV transfer. If the timeout expires, all pending transfer requests are cancelled and an error response is sent. This affects throughput by determining how long the system waits before aborting stalled transfers.
On Ascend NPU, the primary performance impact is on memory management in disaggregated serving scenarios. The parameter does not directly affect compute throughput or latency for individual requests, but improper tuning can lead to memory pressure (too high) or unnecessary request aborts (too low), indirectly affecting overall throughput.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_MULTI_STREAM_GEMM_TOKEN_THRESHOLD
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls a token-count threshold for enabling multi-stream overlap of the attention input GEMM with auxiliary GEMMs in DeepSeek-V4 models. When the number of tokens in the batch is at or below this threshold, the FP8 main GEMM has idle SMs that can be shared with bf16 auxiliary GEMMs (e.g., indexer weights and kv-score projections), providing a 5-45% latency improvement. Above the threshold, the FP8 GEMM saturates the device and cross-stream synchronization becomes pure overhead. The parameter is read at vllm/envs.py:1698 and used at vllm/model_executor/layers/ deepseek_v4_attention.py:411 to gate the `execute_in_parallel` call. On Ascend NPU, this parameter is not overridden by vllm-ascend and follows upstream behavior, but its effectiveness depends on whether the Da Vinci architecture exhibits similar SM saturation characteristics as CUDA GPUs. The impact is limited to DeepSeek-V4 model architectures only.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls how transformer layers are distributed across pipeline-parallel (PP) stages. When set, it overrides the default even-distribution algorithm in get_pp_indices() (vllm/distributed/utils.py:111-140). The value is a comma-separated string of integers, where each integer specifies the number of hidden layers assigned to the corresponding PP rank. The number of entries must equal pp_size, and the sum must equal num_hidden_layers. On Ascend NPU, pipeline parallelism is commonly used to split large models across multiple devices when tensor parallelism alone is insufficient. An imbalanced partition can cause one PP stage to become a bottleneck (reducing throughput) or to exceed NPU memory limits (causing OOM). The default algorithm places extra layers on middle partitions to balance compute while accounting for embedding layers on the first/last stages. Manual tuning via this env var allows Ascend users to optimize for specific model architectures where the default heuristic may not be optimal, such as models with unusually large embedding layers or non-uniform layer costs. The partition also affects the AOT compilation cache key (vllm/compilation/caching.py:568), meaning different partition strings will trigger recompilation.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_RAY_DP_PACK_STRATEGY
legacy_profiles.impact_detail:
This environment variable controls how data-parallel (DP) ranks are packed onto Ray nodes when using the Ray-based data-parallel backend. The packing strategy directly affects inter-node communication patterns and resource utilization, which in turn impacts throughput and latency on Ascend NPU clusters.
Three strategies are available: - "\"strict\": Allocates exactly data-parallel-size-local DP ranks to each selected node."
  This ensures predictable, balanced placement and is required for DeepEP all-to-all
  backends (deepep_high_throughput, deepep_low_latency) which mandate that EP ranks
  [0,7], [8,15], etc. reside on the same node.
- "\"fill\": For the DP master node, allocates exactly data-parallel-size-local DP ranks;"
  for non-master nodes, allocates as many DP ranks as can fit. This can lead to
  unbalanced placement and is incompatible with DeepEP backends.
- "\"span\": Allocates one DP rank across as many nodes as required for the configured"
  world_size. Should only be used when a single DP rank requires multiple nodes
  (i.e., when world_size exceeds the maximum device count per node). Uses Ray's
  "PACK" placement strategy instead of "STRICT_PACK".

On Ascend NPU multi-node deployments, the choice of packing strategy affects HCCL communication topology. "strict" placement keeps DP groups within single nodes where possible, minimizing cross-node HCCL traffic. "span" forces cross-node communication for every DP group, which can significantly increase latency due to inter-node network bandwidth limitations. "fill" may create asymmetric communication patterns where some nodes handle more DP ranks than others, leading to load imbalance.
This parameter is ignored when data-parallel-backend is not "ray".

Checks if strategy is "span" to default data_parallel_size_local to 1 when DP ranks span multiple nodes.

No vllm-ascend override was found, so the upstream behavior applies directly to Ascend deployments using Ray.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_RPC_TIMEOUT
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: VLLM_RPC_TIMEOUT controls the timeout (in milliseconds) for ZMQ RPC calls between the vLLM frontend/API server and the backend engine processes. On Ascend NPU, this timeout applies to simple data operations (as noted in the source comment: "Time in ms for the zmq client to wait for a response from the backend server for simple data operations"). If the timeout is too low, RPC calls may fail prematurely during periods of high system load or when the NPU driver is busy, causing request failures or engine restarts. If set too high, it may delay error detection. This parameter does not directly affect token generation throughput or NPU compute efficiency, but it can impact end-to-end latency under load by causing unnecessary retries or failures. vllm-ascend does not override or modify this parameter; the upstream vLLM ZMQ communication layer is used as-is on Ascend.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM_TOKEN_THRESHOLD
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: Controls whether shared experts in MoE models (e.g., DeepSeek-V2/V3) execute in a separate CUDA stream overlapping with the main computation. When the number of tokens in the batch is at or below this threshold, shared experts run in an auxiliary stream (MULTI_STREAM_OVERLAPPED mode), allowing overlap with the main expert computation. Above the threshold, the overhead of input cloning and cross-stream synchronization outweighs the overlap benefit, so shared experts run sequentially (NO_OVERLAP mode). On Ascend NPU, the effectiveness depends on whether the CANN runtime and HCCL communication patterns benefit from stream-level parallelism. The code path is in `_determine_shared_experts_order()` at vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/runner/shared_experts.py:106, which checks `current_platform.is_cuda()` — this means the multi-stream path is only active on CUDA-like platforms. Ascend NPU may or may not satisfy this check depending on how vllm-ascend registers its platform. If the platform check fails, this parameter has no effect on Ascend. If it passes, tuning this threshold can reduce latency for small-to-medium batch sizes by overlapping shared expert computation with other operations.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_SKIP_P2P_CHECK
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls whether vLLM performs an actual GPU peer-to-peer (P2P) access check during custom allreduce initialization. When VLLM_SKIP_P2P_CHECK is true (the default), vLLM trusts the driver's P2P capability report and skips the runtime verification via gpu_p2p_access_check(). When set to false, vLLM performs an explicit P2P access test between each pair of GPUs in the world. On Ascend NPU, this code path is in the upstream vllm custom_all_reduce module, which is GPU-specific (uses torch.cuda). vllm-ascend does not override or reference this variable — it uses HCCL-based communication instead of custom allreduce. Therefore, this parameter has minimal impact on Ascend NPU: the custom allreduce path is typically not exercised on Ascend hardware, making the P2P check irrelevant for most Ascend deployments. However, if custom allreduce is somehow enabled on Ascend (unusual), setting this to false would add a small initialization-time overhead from the P2P verification loop.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_USE_AOT_COMPILE
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: VLLM_USE_AOT_COMPILE controls whether vLLM performs Ahead-of-Time (AOT) compilation of torch.compile graphs during the model warmup phase, caching the compiled artifacts for reuse on subsequent invocations. When enabled (value "1"), the compilation overhead is shifted from the first inference request to the warmup phase, and subsequent requests benefit from pre-compiled, optimized kernels. This directly affects cold-start latency (first request latency), steady-state throughput (by avoiding JIT compilation pauses), and memory usage (compiled artifacts are cached to disk under VLLM_CACHE_ROOT/torch_compile_cache/torch_aot_compile/). The default value is dynamically computed: "it defaults to \"1\" when PyTorch >= 2.10.0 and" VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE is not set, otherwise "0". On Ascend NPU, this parameter is upstream-only (no vllm-ascend override found in the provided context), but its effect depends on the Ascend torch.compile backend (torch_npu). The AOT path in vllm/compilation/decorators.py:525-574 generates a hash from compilation factors, checks for cached artifacts, and either loads them or triggers fresh compilation. In vllm/compilation/wrapper.py:138-145, when enabled, it patches torch._dynamo.config.enable_aot_compile=True before calling torch.compile. The compiled callable is stored as self.aot_compiled_fn and invoked directly on subsequent calls, bypassing the normal torch.compile guard mechanism. This significantly reduces per-request overhead but requires sufficient disk space for cache storage and may increase warmup time on first run.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_USE_MEGA_AOT_ARTIFACT
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: When enabled (set to "1"), VLLM_USE_MEGA_AOT_ARTIFACT changes how compiled model artifacts are loaded from the disk cache. Instead of re-splitting graph modules and running aot_autograd on each subgraph during warm start, it reconstructs the serializable function directly from standalone compile artifacts via `reconstruct_serializable_fn_from_mega_artifact` (vllm/compilation/caching.py:319-333). This eliminates aot_autograd passes on subgraphs entirely — tests confirm 0 aot_autograd invocations vs 30 without the flag (tests/compile/h100/test_startup.py:80-88). The result is significantly faster model loading and warm-start time, which directly reduces end-to-end latency for cold/warm starts. It also affects the compilation cache key by including inductor factors (vllm/compilation/caching.py:578-579) and disables `bundled_autograd_cache` in functorch config (vllm/compilation/compiler_interface.py:165-166). Requires PyTorch >= 2.10.0 for the `aot` parameter in `standalone_compile`; falls back to non-AOT mode with a warning on older versions (vllm/compilation/compiler_interface.py:305-311). On Ascend NPU, this parameter is upstream-only — no vllm-ascend override was found in the provided context, so its behavior depends on whether the Ascend PyTorch build meets the version requirement and whether `torch._inductor.standalone_compile` is available.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_USE_RAY_COMPILED_DAG_CHANNEL_TYPE
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls the communication channel type used by Ray Compiled Graph for pipeline-parallel (PP) stage communication. On Ascend NPU, the Ray compiled-graph executor path is NOT the default — vLLM on Ascend typically uses the multiprocessing-based executor (VLLM_USE_RAY_V2_EXECUTOR_BACKEND defaults to 1 in upstream, and Ascend does not override this). The compiled-graph path is only activated when distributed_executor_backend="ray" AND VLLM_USE_RAY_V2_EXECUTOR_BACKEND=0. In that specific configuration, this env var determines whether PP communication uses NCCL (via cupy), shared memory (shm), or auto-detection. On Ascend, NCCL is not available — the platform uses HCCL instead. The code at vllm/v1/executor/ray_executor.py:74-75 shows that for TPU/XPU platforms, the channel type is forcibly set to "shm" because NCCL is NVIDIA-specific. Ascend NPU is neither TPU nor XPU, so this auto-override does NOT apply. If a user explicitly sets this to "nccl" on Ascend, it will fail at vllm/v1/executor/ray_executor.py:537-542 because cupy (required for NCCL channel) is not installed or compatible with Ascend. The "auto" default will likely select "shm" on Ascend since NCCL is unavailable. Performance impact is low because: (1) the compiled-graph path is rarely used on Ascend, and (2) when used, the effective choice is almost always "shm", which has minimal tuning headroom.

In the vLLM v1 executor (vllm/v1/executor/ray_executor.py:636), the value is passed as `_overlap_gpu_communication` to `forward_dag.experimental_compile()`. This instructs Ray to overlap inter-worker communication with computation during compiled graph execution. The parameter is logged at executor initialization (ray_executor.py:566) but has no vllm-ascend-specific override or handling. Performance impact is low because: "(1) it only applies when using the Ray" compiled graph executor backend (not the default RayExecutorV2), (2) the feature is marked experimental, and (3) on Ascend NPU, HCCL overlap behavior may differ from GPU NCCL and is not explicitly tuned.

legacy_profiles.name: VLLM_USE_RAY_V2_EXECUTOR_BACKEND
legacy_profiles.impact_detail: This environment variable controls which Ray-based distributed executor vLLM uses when `distributed_executor_backend="ray"`. When set to 1 (default), vLLM uses `RayExecutorV2`, a message-queue-based executor. When set to 0, vLLM uses `RayDistributedExecutor`, which leverages Ray's Compiled Graph (previously known as Ray DAG) for communication. The choice of executor backend directly affects how workers communicate during distributed inference, which impacts scheduling overhead, inter-worker latency, and overall throughput. On Ascend NPU, the executor backend interacts with HCCL communication primitives — the compiled-graph backend may have different HCCL integration characteristics compared to the MQ-based V2 backend. Note: "vllm-ascend does not override this parameter, but the underlying HCCL" communication layer on Ascend may behave differently from NCCL on GPU, so the performance tradeoffs between the two backends may differ from upstream GPU behavior.

usage_locations.context: In the v1 engine executor selection logic, when distributed_executor_backend is "ray", this env var determines whether to instantiate RayExecutorV2 (MQ-based) or RayDistributedExecutor (compiled-graph backend).
Declared as a typed environment variable in the VllmEnv class with default False (but the actual env var default is "1" via the lambda in envs.py:786).

related_parameters.name: distributed_executor_backend
related_parameters.relation: This env var only takes effect when distributed_executor_backend is set to "ray". If the backend is "mp", "uni", or a custom Executor subclass, this env var is ignored.

related_parameters.name: VLLM_USE_RAY_COMPILED_DAG_OVERLAP_COMM
